original_value: 3D weaving is an emerging technology for manufacturing multilayer woven textiles. In this work, we present Weavecraft: an interactive, simulation-based design tool for 3D weaving. Unlike existing textile software that uses 2D representations for design patterns, we propose a novel weave block representation that helps the user to understand 3D woven structures and to create complex multi-layered patterns. With Weavecraft, users can create blocks either from scratch or by loading traditional weaves, compose the blocks into large structures, and edit the pattern at various scales. Furthermore, users can verify the design with a physically based simulator, which predicts and visualizes the geometric structure of the woven material and reveals potential defects at an interactive rate. We demonstrate a range of results created with our tool, from simple two-layer cloth and well known 3D structures to a more sophisticated design of a 3D woven shoe, and we evaluate the effectiveness of our system via a formative user study.

result.paraphrase: 3D weaving is an emerging method for producing multilayer woven textiles. In this work, we introduce Weavecraft, an interactive design tool for 3D weaving based on simulation. Unlike current textile software that relies on 2D pattern representations, we present a new weave block representation that helps users understand 3D woven structures and build complex multilayer patterns. With Weavecraft, users can create blocks from scratch or load traditional weaves, combine blocks into larger structures, and modify patterns at multiple scales. In addition, users can validate their designs with a physics-based simulator that predicts and visualizes the geometric structure of the woven material and exposes possible defects at interactive speed. We show a variety of results produced with our tool, ranging from simple two-layer cloth and well-known 3D structures to a more advanced 3D woven shoe design, and we assess the system’s effectiveness through a formative user study.
